LESSON: LINEAR EQUATIONS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra 2.1 Algebraic Expressions (5 lessons) • simple algebraic statements • si
Topic 2.2: Linear Equations

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Linear Equations. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we use linear equations in real-life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form linear equations in one unknown in different situations
2. solve linear equations in one unknown in different situations
3. apply linear equations in one unknown to real-life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Linear Equations.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Linear Equations using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Role play activities involving equations with one unknown for example weighing using beam balance. Also, dramatise shopping activities.
2. Discuss how to form and solve linear equations generated from role play activities
3. Communication and Collaboration: speaking, listening and teamwork as the learner role plays activities involving equations in one unknown.
4. Self-efficacy: self-awareness skills as the learner carries out weighing using beam balance and role play different activities.
5. Learning to learn: organising own learning as the learner applies linear equations in real-life. Values

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we use linear equations in real-life?
2. Why do we use linear equations in real-life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Linear Equations is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
